steps.title: The third mini recital
steps.body:
Same shape as the last two recitals: two pieces, names said, hands in frame, one question from the family. This time, phrasing is the thing to carry into the room.

1. Choose the two pieces, one from this sprint and one older.
2. Run each once a day, marking and playing its phrase endings.
3. Decide the slip plan and say it out loud before you play: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar.
4. On recital day, say each name, play with the breaths you practised, hold the last note, and bow.
5. The family asks one question. Answer it, then write the Practice log.

A recital with phrasing sounds like someone telling a story, not someone reciting a list of correct notes. That difference is the whole point of the last five weeks.

figure.alt: A bar of four beats ending in a held note, matching the checklist's own line: last note held, hands off, then a bow.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Two pieces chosen, one from this sprint and one older
Each piece run once a day, phrase endings marked and practised
Slip plan said out loud: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar
Last note held, hands off, then a bow
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, names said out loud, phone where it sees the hands. Slips stay in.
